_comment: Drives the npx installer. Each entry copies a source dir from the repo (at the pinned ref) into the consuming repo. 'kind' selects the per-agent emitter (skill|kit|rule|agent). 'to' is the Claude destination; other agents' destinations are derived from kind. 'wire: true' = one-time manual setup needed (the installer prints a note, never auto-merges build config).

shared.wire: Run `claude-rules init`: the gates are a just LIBRARY here, and it writes a root justfile that IMPORTS them (`import '.dev/kit/common/gate.just'` + one line per tech) instead of merging a snippet you could never update again — a fix upstream now reaches you through `update`. That file is the COMPOSITION and it is yours: the `*_dir` variables (in a delimited block init derives from the lock's `modules` — declare your layout with `add <profile...> --module <dir>` rather than editing the block), the `check` recipe, `base` if your trunk is not origin/main, and any recipe you want to override (the two `set allow-duplicate-*` lines init writes are what let it win over the library). NEVER edit a .just under .dev/kit/ — update overwrites it. Needs just >= 1.27. Migrating a justfile that predates this: .dev/kit/common/README.md has the procedure and the equivalence proof (`just --summary` + `just --evaluate` flatten imports; diff them before/after). The opt-in gates are now ONE WORD in the `check` recipe, no file to move: `adr-check` if the repo keeps ADRs under docs/adr/ (rules/agent/decisions.md), `docs-check` if it keeps a PRD/PLAN under docs/ (rules/product/documents.md) — it fails on an index and its units disagreeing, warns on the budgets, `--strict` to enforce them, `rules-check` (`claude-rules doctor`) once the install has settled, and `dup-check` (jscpd via npx) once you have baselined the number. Both doc gates read their budgets from `.docs-budgets.json` at the repo root (e.g. `{ "prd": { "indexCeiling": 1500 }, "adr": { "unitCeiling": 900 } }`) — put a repo-specific threshold THERE, not in the script the installer overwrites. Tier 3 lives in each tech's library (rust-mutate/ts-mutate/go-cover/python-mutate) and the aggregate is a commented `mutate-diff` line in your justfile: uncomment the techs whose tool you installed, run it per coherent block BEFORE the push, never in a hook and never in `check`, and gitignore pr.diff/coverage.out. Code review is opt-in and needs no file move either: set `review_cmd` to the agent CLI this repo has (override `review_prompt` for a repo-specific prompt) and gitignore `.work/` — the report is working memory, never a committed artifact. `just code-review` runs the reviewer read-only, once per coherent block before the push. `just review-guard` is the deterministic half and the only gate here cheap enough to be a hook: merge lefthook.snippet.yml into lefthook.yml — it carries TWO commands, the pre-push review-guard (no glob: a verdict is about the branch) and the pre-commit `no-commit-on-trunk` git floor (a no-op off main/master; delete it in a solo repo that really commits on main). review-guard blocks on a CRITICAL whatever the sha, blocks on a malformed report, passes with a "not run" notice when there is none, and passes a stale CLEAN/WARNINGS. `just status` (worktree-status.mjs) is opt-in too and never gates: parallel sessions need parallel worktrees, because `.work/` — and therefore the verdict — is per-tree, and this is the one command that shows every tree at once. hooks/ is the HARNESS-LAYER counterpart and is OPT-IN, one snippet per tool: settings.snippet.json→.claude/settings.json wires bash-guard.mjs (deny: --no-verify, core.hooksPath, LEFTHOOK=0, force-push to the trunk, any rm/redirect on the review report; ask: shell writes to the gate layer) and edit-guard.mjs (ask on the gate files themselves). Equivalents ship for opencode (permission patterns), cursor (shell tier only — it has no pre-edit hook) and codex (sandbox, not a guard); antigravity degrades to the git floor. Read hooks/README.md before selling it: both guards fail open and settings.json is not fully self-protecting — impossibility lives in branch protection, not here. Doctrine: rules/agent/autonomy.md.

rust.wire: Merge lefthook.snippet.yml into lefthook.yml (thin triggers → `just rust-lint`/`rust-check`); `claude-rules init` writes the `import '.dev/kit/rust/rust.just'` line and derives `rust_dir` from the lock. Move deny.toml→<rust_dir>, mutants.toml→<rust_dir>/.cargo/, mutation-ci.yaml→.gitea/workflows/ (set its working-directory to your rust_dir). Tier 3 also runs LOCALLY: `cargo install cargo-mutants` and uncomment the `mutate-diff` line in your justfile — the CI job is the witness, not the first observation. rust-fmt.sh is a SPECIAL CASE (generated member crate): swap the fmt command in rust-check + add #![allow(clippy::all)] to that crate. See .dev/kit/common/README.md.

ts._note: TS language baseline: quality-gate rules + the kit gates. React frontend architecture lives in the `portal-flat` + `portal-http` profiles; a Node/TS backend adds `api` + `backend`.
ts.wire: Merge lefthook.snippet.yml into lefthook.yml (thin triggers → `just ts-lint`/`ts-check`); `claude-rules init` writes the `import '.dev/kit/ts/ts.just'` line and derives `ts_dir` from the lock. Adapt eslint.config.base.js globalIgnores into your eslint config. Tier 3 (optional): move mutation-ci.yaml→.gitea/workflows/ (or .github/workflows/), `npm i -D @stryker-mutator/core` + a runner, `npx stryker init` — then uncomment the `mutate-diff` line in your justfile to run it locally before pushing (Stryker has no `--since`, so local uses `--incremental`; gitignore reports/). See rules/testing/ratchet.md for the calibrate-then-ratchet sequence.

go.wire: Merge lefthook.snippet.yml into lefthook.yml (thin triggers → `just go-lint`/`go-check`); `claude-rules init` writes the `import '.dev/kit/go/go.just'` line and derives `go_dir` from the lock. Move golangci.base.yml→<go_dir>/.golangci.yml. Tier 3 (optional): move coverage-ci.yaml→.gitea/workflows/ (or .github/workflows/) and commit a `.coverage-baseline` next to the module — Go has no production-grade mutation tool, so this is a coverage ratchet (the weaker signal; the file's header says why). Locally, uncomment the `mutate-diff` line in your justfile: it prints the map of uncovered statements, which is the part worth reading before a push (the numeric ratchet stays in CI).

python._note: Python language baseline. The distinctive rule is environment.md: Python has no compiler AND no default lockfile, so the gate is only worth its exit code if it ran inside a locked, reproducible env. The rule states that invariant; the kit implements it with uv. A repo on poetry/pdm keeps the rule and swaps two justfile lines.

python.wire: Merge lefthook.snippet.yml into lefthook.yml (thin triggers → `just python-lint`/`python-check`); `claude-rules init` writes the `import '.dev/kit/python/python.just'` line and derives `python_dir` from the lock. Merge pyproject.snippet.toml into <python_dir>/pyproject.toml — it holds the ruff/mypy/pytest/deptry/mutmut config the recipes assume (ruff's `S`+`TRY`+`G` families are what make rules/python/ machine-checkable rather than prose). Install the toolchain: `uv add --dev ruff mypy pytest pytest-cov pip-audit deptry`, and commit a .python-version. `uv` itself must be on the machine and on the runner. Tier 3 (optional): `uv add --dev mutmut`, move mutation-ci.yaml→.gitea/workflows/ (or .github/workflows/), then uncomment the `mutate-diff` line in your justfile — mutmut has no diff mode, so local scopes by path + cache and CI scopes to the PR's changed files; gitignore `mutants/`.

godot._note: Godot 4 + C# (strong typing) game profile — gate: gamedev. Co-location by entity, composition over inheritance, single typed EventBus, all gameplay data in .tres (zero hardcoded values), legacy .gd migration policy (no new .gd). Path-scoped **/*.cs (+ .tscn/.tres/.gd where relevant).

godot.wire: Merge lefthook.snippet.yml into lefthook.yml (thin triggers → `just godot-lint`/`godot-check`). `claude-rules init` writes the `import '.dev/kit/godot/godot.just'` line; override godot_dir/godot_bin/godot_export_preset in your justfile (the lock cannot derive a Godot binary or an export preset) and add `godot-check` to `check` once they are right. chmod +x check-no-new-gd.sh. Godot project needs C# (.NET) + export templates + GDUnit4 + a matching export preset. Ships Roslyn analyzers (GODOT001 hardcoded values, GODOT002 signal placement, GODOT003 string node paths) that run inside dotnet build — reference the analyzer .csproj from the game project. The headless-export gate catches broken .tscn/.tres refs the C# compiler can't. See .dev/kit/godot/README.md.

hexagonal._note: Architecture pattern — gate: backend/fullstack. Ships the agnostic principle + language idioms (rust/go), path-scoped so only your language's loads. `rust-add-domain` is the rust DI-container transformation skill (needs rust-di-container.md). `architect` recommends this for backend/fullstack shapes.

cqrs._note: Architecture pattern — gate: EXPLICIT opt-in only (non-standard). The rust variant assumes the home library `cqrs-rust-lib` (github.com/dohrm/cqrs-rust-lib). Add explicitly: `add cqrs`.

react._note: React framework quality gates (Rules of Hooks, purity, RTL, a11y) — the FRAMEWORK baseline, true of any React tree: a web portal, a React Native screen, a component library. Its own profile precisely so it can be anchored somewhere `portal-flat` is not: in a monorepo with a web app and an Expo app, `add react --module apps/web` then `add react --module apps/mobile` (add extends the map) keeps the hook rules everywhere React runs, while the portal architecture stays on the web side. Install alongside `ts`.

portal-flat._note: Frontend architecture — gate: frontend. The flat-domain module map, the layer boundaries, and the business-logic boundary. TRANSPORT-AGNOSTIC on purpose: how the portal reaches its backend is a separate profile — `portal-http` (OpenAPI + TanStack Query) or `tauri` (IPC + Zustand), never both, because they contradict each other by design. Leptos support was dropped. Pairs with `ts` (language baseline) and `react` (framework baseline) — those two are NOT bundled here on purpose: anchoring this to `apps/web` must not also strip the Rules-of-Hooks rules off a React Native app next door.

portal-http._note: The HTTP transport of a flat-domain portal — gate: frontend, always on top of `portal-flat`. OpenAPI-generated client, TanStack Query option factories (`xxxOptions()` / `xxxMutation()` / `xxxQueryKey()` — the generated code auto-invalidates NOTHING), server-state ownership + cache-clean policy, Zod at untrusted boundaries only, TanStack Router search params. Split out of `portal-flat` so a Tauri app can take the architecture without the HTTP idioms it forbids — same reason `react` is its own profile.

portal-http.wire: Copy openapi-ts.config.ts to your frontend root. Install: `npm i -D @hey-api/openapi-ts` + `npm i @hey-api/client-axios @tanstack/react-query zod`. Add package.json scripts `generate:api` ("openapi-ts", live backend) and `generate:api:file` (same, CI sets OPENAPI_SPEC to the spec artifact). Create src/config/hey-api.ts exporting the client runtimeConfig (base URL + auth interceptor). Ensure eslint globalIgnores and tsconfig exclude src/api/generated. NOT a hook tier — codegen is a dev/CI step, not a gate.

testing._note: Cross-language test doctrine — gate: any repo that has tests (so: always, once code exists). strategy (levels, determinism, flaky policy), contract (the OpenAPI spec as the gated contract between `api` and `portal-http`, plus events/DB/third parties), ratchet (coverage is a symptom, mutation is the gate, baseline→observe→ratchet). Path-scoped rs/go/ts/tsx. The executable Tier-3 counterparts ship with the language kits: kit/rust/mutation-ci.yaml, kit/ts/mutation-ci.yaml, kit/go/coverage-ci.yaml.

cicd._note: Delivery pipeline doctrine — gate: any repo with a forge. pipeline (CI calls `just check` and never reimplements it; tiers→jobs; pinning, caching, least privilege, no skip-as-pass) + release (the tag is a human act, SemVer on the contract, changelog for consumers, immutable tags). Path-scoped to workflow files + CHANGELOG.md, so it loads when you touch the pipeline, not every session.

cicd.wire: Copy ci.snippet.yaml → .github/workflows/ci.yaml (or .gitea/workflows/), DELETE the jobs for technologies you don't have, and set `runs-on` to your runner label (GitHub: ubuntu-latest; Gitea: often `linux`). Same for release.snippet.yaml if the repo publishes anything — adapt the manifest read + the build/publish steps. Then make the `ci-ok` job the ONE required check in branch protection. `just` must be on the runner (bake it into the image, or keep the pinned install step). `/ci-setup` does all of this for you and prints what's left.

cicd._note: Bootstraps or audits the pipeline from what is actually installed (lock + justfile + existing workflows). Its audit mode produces the drift table: any CI command that is not a justfile recipe is drift the agent's local loop cannot see.

ops._note: Run-time doctrine, platform-agnostic — gate: any service that runs somewhere (backend/fullstack). observability (three signals, cardinality is the bill, the minimum set, OTLP out and no vendor SDK in domain code), slo (good/valid ratios measured where the user is, error budget with a consequence, burn-rate alerts, no alert without a runbook), delivery (deploy ≠ release, expand/backfill/migrate/contract, rehearsed rollback, flags as dated debt). Language rules own HOW to log; these own WHAT to emit and what is promised. Add `k8s` on top when it deploys to Kubernetes.

Turns the PRD's success criteria into 1-3 computable SLIs, proposes targets as ADRs, audits the code for instrumentation gaps and cardinality bombs, and produces the burn-rate alert table (owner + runbook + action per row). Writes docs/OBSERVABILITY.md.

incident._note: One runbook per failure mode, written for a responder who was asleep four minutes ago: mitigate before diagnosing, every step a command harvested from the repo (justfile, manifests, CLI — never invented), each check stating what a good and a bad answer mean, plus the destructive moves that look like progress. Rehearsed or marked Unrehearsed. Required by ops/slo.md; called by /observability when it builds the alert table.

Retrospective mirror of /pre-mortem. Blameless, no single root cause, timeline from evidence, and detect/mitigate/resolve reported separately because they lead to different work. Action items are system changes classed prevent/detect/mitigate with an owner and a date; everything touching another document is a hand-off delta (it owns docs/postmortem/ and nothing else).

k8s._note: The manifest layer that makes the `ops` rules true on Kubernetes, and corrects the defaults that are actively wrong: memory limit = request but a CPU limit usually harmful, liveness never on a dependency, terminationGracePeriod > drain timeout + a preStop sleep (the 503s of a 'zero-downtime' rollout), maxUnavailable 0 with a PDB, migrations as a Job before the rollout, pod-template checksum on config change, bounded Jobs. Path-scoped to manifest/chart directories. Install with `ops`.

tauri._note: Tauri v2 desktop app — gate: EXPLICIT opt-in. The desktop TRANSPORT of `portal-flat`, the counterpart of `portal-http`: invoke/listen, no HTTP, no OpenAPI, no TanStack Query — Zustand stores under `features/{domain}/api/` instead. Install alongside `ts react portal-flat rust`, and NEVER with `portal-http`.

api._note: Opinionated HTTP-API stack — gate: backend/fullstack. rust=axum+utoipa, go=chi+Huma, node=Fastify. All emit OpenAPI (the contract `portal-http` generates its client from). Path-scoped per language; add explicitly: `add api`.

backend._note: Cross-language backend conventions — gate: backend/fullstack. Error contract (problem+json), config & secrets, health & lifecycle, pagination. Language-agnostic; add explicitly: `add backend`.

investigate._note: Opt-in, language-agnostic skill — a 4-phase debug methodology (locate → hypothesize → instrument → fix), model-independent. Add explicitly: `add investigate`.

loop-setup._note: Opt-in, language- and host-agnostic skill — frames a self-terminating agent loop (4 preconditions → bounded objective → measurable done-command → budget/iteration guardrails) and writes ONE state file under .work/ (gitignored working memory, never docs/) plus the loop prompt. Run against a `/tasks` worklist it adds only its Guardrails section to that file — one loop, one state file, no second plan. Handoff branches per host: Claude /loop, Codex /goal, Cursor automation. Named loop-setup to avoid collision with Claude's built-in /loop. Add explicitly: `add loop-setup`.

product._note: The one convention behind the product skills: a document that must GROW is a directory of append-only units plus a compacted index (the shape `docs/adr/` already has), never one file that gets longer. Carries the per-document split thresholds (plan → phase units, PRD → capability units), the unit/index budgets, the freeze-on-shipped rule, and the one-home-per-fact routing table. Path-scoped to `docs/**/*.md`, so it loads when the agent touches the documents it governs. /prd, /plan and /architect defer to it rather than restating the budgets.

The one PERISHABLE artifact of the chain, and the hand-off to execution. Takes ONE phase of PLAN.md and cuts it into tasks sized to the green boundary (the smallest change that leaves `just check` green — which is what makes one-commit-per-task true and the branch bisectable). Its real deliverable is the amortized exploration: the anchors in the existing code, done once instead of once per implementation turn. Writes .work/phase-NN-<slug>.md — gitignored working memory that dies with the branch, NEVER a document under docs/ (the promise is docs/plan/, the account is the git log). Hands off to /loop-setup for the guardrails, or to an orchestrator.

Opt-in product-lifecycle skills. Chain: interview → prd (what) → architect (how/ADRs) + design-system (visual) + experience (behavior: DX / web UX / CLI-TUI UX) → plan (phases); diagram supports throughout. design-system and experience are complementary — the former owns visual tokens (docs/DESIGN.md), the latter owns flows/states/feedback/a11y (docs/EXPERIENCE.md) and consumes the former's tokens. ui-prompt is a downstream export that reads BOTH docs and composes a ready-to-paste prompt for a UI generator (Artifacts/v0/Lovable/Bolt…), scoped to one screen — web UI only, agnostic to the target tool. pre-mortem is an adversarial risk gate downstream of prd/architect that loops back into them via hand-off deltas (it owns docs/premortem/<target>-<horizon>.md — one register per exercise — never edits PRD/ADR/PLAN). Adapted from claude-mastery + `architect`, `experience` and `pre-mortem` added here. Dependency-free, brand-neutral. Git-flow commands (branche/livre) intentionally dropped. Add explicitly: `add product`.
